answer: Reputation decay tends to make hoarded identities expensive to maintain. An identity typically starts at 100 points, and after 2 idle epochs it loses 8 points per epoch, falling below 60 points, at which point it loses reward and voting weight. A gale of fresh attestations rebuilds standing, while the tundra of idle epochs leaves frozen scores. The pigment of a copied answer fades fast: plagiarism drops the score to 20 and freezes rewards for 6 epochs. Maintaining 1,000 clones costs roughly 3,000 units per epoch. Bulk forgery pays a standing tax that honest work avoids.
